sentences.text: This claim petition emanates in respect of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner by name Sri Prabhakar in respect of the Road Traffic Accident dated 21.02.2020.

2. Succinctly stated the facts germane to the lis involved in this petition are briefly summarized as follows:
That on 21.02.2020 at about 12.30 p.m when the petitioner was proceeding in his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-08-K-8694 and when he reached near Karumariyamma Temple, Whitefield, Bengaluru, at that time, respondent's motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AF-2050 was driven by its rider in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.

Due to which, petitioner fell down on the road, at that time, driver of the Mahindra Bolero goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-C- 8670 (herein after referred to as the offending vehicle) was driven in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and SCCH 15 4 MVC No.2284/2020
ran over left leg of the petitioner, resulting in the accident.
Due to the impact, Petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Respondent No.1 filed Written Statement contending as follows:
It is submitted by the respondent No.1 that the alleged accident never took place due to the negligence on the part of this respondent.
Further submitted that this respondent has not driven in a rash or negligent manner.
The petitioner has not observed the vehicle proceeding in the main road, he suddenly stopped his vehicle,
accident took place purely due to SCCH 15 5 MVC No.2284/2020 the negligence of petitioner and not the negligence of the rider of the offending motorcycle.
It is submitted that the offending vehicle is insured with respondent No.2.

It is submitted that the amount claimed by the petitioners is highly exorbitant, excessive, arbitrary,
unreasonable and without any legal basis.
Hence, on these grounds, Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the petition against him.

The Respondent No.2 has filed written statement submitting as follows:
The respondent No.2 admitted that it has issued insurance policy to the offending motorcycle in favour of the respondent No.1.
Without prejudice the liability of the respondent No.2 if any is subject to the validity of driving license and terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
The rider of the said motorcycle vehicle did not have valid and effective driving license.
It is denied that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle.
The age, avocation of the petitioner is denied.
SCCH 15 6 MVC No.2284/2020 Hence, on these grounds Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

Respondent No.4 filed Written Statement contending as follows:
The respondent No.4 admitted that it has issued insurance policy to the offending Bolero Goods vehicle in favour of the respondent No.3.
Without prejudice the liability of the respondent No.4 if any is subject to the validity of driving license and terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
The driver of the said vehicle did not have valid and effective driving license.
It is denied that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car.
It is submitted that the alleged accident took place due to the sole negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The age, avocation of the petitioner is denied.
Hence, on these grounds Respondent No.4 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

Vide order dated 04.03.2021 the following issues were framed by this Tribunal :-
ISSUES
1 ) Whether the petitioner proves that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of riding of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AF-2050 and as a result, he sustained injuries?

2) Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
3) What Order or Award?

6. In support of the claimants, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and examined one witness as PW.2 and relied upon Ex.P.1 to Ex.P-15 documents and respondent No.4 examined one witness as RW.1 and respondent No.2 examined one witness as RW.2 and relied upon Ex.R1 and 2 documents.
SCCH 15 8 MVC No.2284/2020 7.
Oral submissions were advanced by Ld. Counsel for parties in this case.

Having perused the records my issue wise findings run as under:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3 : As per the Final Order

for the following :
 REASONS  8.
Issue No.1:
Before adjudication of the issue with respect to the compensation it is quintessential to adjudicate on the issue of negligence.

It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AF-2050 and driver of the Bolero Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-C-8670 / offending vehicle.

9. In this regard the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and in his chief-examination he has deposed that on 21.02.2020 at about 12.30 p.m he was proceeding in his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-08-K-8694 and when he SCCH 15 9 MVC No.2284/2020 reached near Karumariyamma Temple, Whitefield, Bengaluru, at that time, rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AF- 2050 drove in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to which, he fell down on the road and at that time, driver of the Mahindra Prabhakar.

Bolero goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-C-8670 was driven in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and ran over the left leg of the petitioner, resulting in the accident due to the impact he sustained grievous injuries.
10.
The petitioner in support of his claim has in addition to describing the course of the accident in line with the facts mentioned in the complaint has relied upon Ex.P1 to 7 documents.

Ex.P1 is the FIR which is registered against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offenses under Sec.279 and 337 of IPC and under Sec.134(A&B) and 187 of MV Act on the basis of the complaint given by petitioner on the same day of the accident as per Ex.P2.

Ex.P3 is the spot mahazar which discloses the spot of the accident near Whitefield main road, in SCCH 15 10 MVC No.2284/2020 front of Ganapathi temple and the width of the road is about 15 meter tar road.
Ex.P4 is the IMV report which discloses the damages sustained to the vehicles in the accident.
Ex.P5 is the spot sketch which shows that the accident occurred in the middle of the road and all three vehicles were proceeding from south towards north side of the road.
Ex.P6 is the wound certificate which discloses that the petitioner sustained injuries due to the impact of the accident.

Ex.P7 is the charge sheet filed after completion of the investigation against the driver of the Bolero Goods vehicle and rider of the motorcycle for the offenses under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC and Sec.138(A&B) r/w Sec.187 of IMV Act.
Hence these documents produced by the petitioner discloses that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the drivers of the offending vehicles.
11. As far as the manner of the accident is concerned PW.1 is cross-examined by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 and 4 and in the cross-examination of PW.1 he has
SCCH 15 11 MVC No.2284/2020 deposed that he possessed DL as on the date of the accident.
The accident road is two way road and denied that accident occurred on the middle of the road.
He has deposed that the motorcycle was coming from behind, hence he had no occasion to notice the motorcycle.
He has denied that he himself rode in a rash and negligent manner and in the process of overtaking another motorcycle which was coming in the left side caused the accident.
He has denied that the accident occurred due to his negligence.

Except the suggestion that the accident has taken place due to the negligence on the petitioner's side, nothing much is elicited in the cross-examination of PW.1 to prove that the accident took place due to the negligence or rashness on the part of petitioner.
The petitioner has clearly and categorically deposed about the manner of the accident.
The oral testimony of PW.1 has stood unrebutted and PW1 has withstood the cross-examination of Respondent No.2 and 4.
There is no material on record which suggests falsity or untruth in the oral testimony of PW.1 as to the facts and SCCH 15 12 MVC No.2284/2020 circumstances surrounding cause of the accident.
PW.1 has also denied the suggestion imputing the cause of the accident due to their own negligence.

The fact that the driver of the offending vehicle has already been charge sheeted for the offenses under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC and under Sec.134(A&B) r/w 187 of IMV Act itself is strong circumstance to support the oral testimony of PW.1.

The certified copies of FIR,
charge sheet, IMV report and Spot mahazar also corroborate the oral testimony of PW.1.
In view of medical records there is no dispute regarding the nature of injuries sustained by PW.1 in the above accident.

In view of the said discussion it is satisfactorily established that PW.1 suffered grievous injuries on account of rashness and negligence of drivers, driving the offending vehicles at the relevant time.

Hence, issue No.1 is answered in favour of the petitioner and in the 'Affirmative'.

sentences.text: Issue No.2:
In view of the findings on issue No.1 in favour of petitioner, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
SCCH 15 13 MVC No.2284/2020 The computation of compensation will have to be decided separately under various heads.
13. MEDICAL OR TREATMENT EXPENSES:

As far as the medical bills are concerned petitioner has produced MLC register extract, police intimation and case sheet marked at Ex.P11 to 13 through PW.2 and also produced Ex.P8 - medical bills, inpatient bills and other medical bills.
As far as the medical bills are concerned, except suggesting that the said bills are created, nothing is elicited to disprove the authenticity of the said bills.
It is also suggested that Ex.P8 - Sl.No.1 bill payment receipt is not produced.
However, there is no evidence to show that said bills are met by mediclaim or any health insurance.
Hence, in the absence of any such evidence the said hospital bills can be taken into consideration to prove the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner.
Hence, in view the said bills produced the petitioner is awarded an amount of Rs.2,64,220/- under this head.
PAIN AND SUFFERING:

As per the medical documents the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries and Ex.P6 discloses that the petitioner has sustained transverse displaced fractures involving the left leg tibia and fibula left leg and he cannot do any work as prior to the accident.
It is not possible to ascertain the quantum of compensation admissible to petitioner for the trauma, pain and sufferings etc., which he actually suffered due to the accidental injuries.

Keeping in view the trauma and nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by him etc., an amount of Rs.60,000/- is awarded to him towards pain and sufferings.
Thus, he is awarded an amount of Rs.60,000/- under this head.
15. LOSS OF ACTUAL EARNINGS:
In his evidence PW.1 has submitted that he was aged about 35 years and he was working as Supervisor and was earning Rs.80,000/- p.m.
The petitioner has not produced any evidence to prove his income and avocation.

In the absence of any material as to the SCCH 15 15 MVC No.2284/2020 monthly earnings of the Petitioner it would be proper to assume the monthly earnings of the petitioner as per the notional income as on the date of the accident.
Taking into consideration the minimum wages and the lok adalath chart the notional income is taken as Rs.14,500/- p.m for the purpose of assessing compensation.

Taking into consideration that the petitioner due to the injuries might not have been in a position to work for at least six months hence, as such the petitioner is entitled to an amount of Rs.14,500 X 6 = 87,000/- under this head.
16. LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS DUE TO DISABILITY:
The Petitioner has not adduced any evidence to show he has sustained permanent disability due to the injuries sustained in the accident and has not examined any Prabhakar.

sentences.text: Hence in the absence of any evidence it has to be concluded that the petitioner has not SCCH 15 16 MVC No.2284/2020 sustained any permanent disability due to the injuries sustained in the accident.
17. Loss of Amenities:

In view of the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, the extent of permanent physical disability and the extended period of medical treatment, the petitioner is granted a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.
18. Attendant's charges, Special diet and Conveyance:
The facts show that physical condition of the petitioner is such that he might have to taken the help of an attendant.
Further, he would be requiring conveyance for movement.
In this regard petitioner has produced Ex.P9 - Invoice.
His avocation has been hit due to his disablement.
He might have spent considerable amount towards special diet during his treatment.
Therefore, petitioner is granted Rs.25,000/- under this head.

19. TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
SCCH 15 17 MVC No.2284/2020 To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering  60,000/-
2. Loss of amenities  20,000/-
3. Loss of income during the laid  87,000/-
up period 4. Attendant's charges, Extra diet,  25,000/-
and conveyance 5.

Medical expenses  2,64,220/-
6. Loss of Future Income ---- Total 4,56,220/-
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of 4,56,220/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

Regarding rate of interest: As far as the rate of interest is concerned the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in SHRIRAM GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. RAJASTAN VS. SMT.
LAXMI reported in 2018 (4) AKR 808 has held that in case of motor accident claims rate of interest SCCH 15 18 MVC No.2284/2020 awarded is 6% per annum and the Hon'ble High court has been consistently granting 6% interest in Motor Vehicles Accident Claims and Compensation cases.

21. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Bolero Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-C-8670 and rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AF-2050.

As per the detailed discussion made in Issue No.1, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the owner of the Bolero Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA- 53-C-8670 attributes 50% of compensation award amount and the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AF-2050 attributes 50% of the compensation amount towards the said accident.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 to 4 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 and 4 are being the insurers liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1 and 3 and have to pay compensation amount SCCH 15 19 MVC No.2284/2020 to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
22. Issue No.3:

Hence, for the foregoing reasons and in view of the above findings on issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of 4,56,220/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 to 4 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the motorcycle, is directed to deposit the SCCH 15 20 MVC No.2284/2020 50% Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
The Respondent No.4 being the insurer of the Bolero vehicle, is directed to deposit the 50% Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be released to the Petitioner by way of E- payment and after proper identification.
The remaining 25% award amount shall be deposited as F.D. in the name of the Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of three years.

The Respondent No.1 to 4 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation amount to the Petitioner.

The Respondent No.4 being the insurer of the Bolero vehicle, is directed to deposit the 50% Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be released to the Petitioner by way of E- payment and after proper identification.
The remaining 25% award amount shall be deposited as F.D. in the name of the Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of three years.
The Advocate fee is fixed at 1,000/-.
